paper_metadata.title: Enhanced tribological performance of Cr-Fe-Ni-based chemically complex alloys via dual heterogeneous precipitates

evidence.quote: dual heterogeneous precipitates were engineered in a Cr29Fe27Ni32Nb6B2 chemically complex alloy (CCA) matrix by leveraging Ti-V and Mo-W solute effects

This study elucidates the microstructural evolution, mechanical properties, and high-temperature tribological behavior of Cr-Fe-Ni-based CCAs incorporating heterogeneous dual precipitates, synthesized via MA and SPS.

parameters.time: 38 h dry milling + 5 h wet milling (45 h total)

evidence.quote: Intermittent dry milling was conducted for 38 hours at 300 r/min, followed by wet milling for 5 hours at 200 r/min using anhydrous ethanol as a process control agent.

The 45-hour milled powders were then consolidated into bulk form using SPS (LABOX-3010KF, Japan) at 1100 ± 15 ℃ for 10 min under a constant pressure of 35 MPa. The average heating rate was 65 ℃ /min, and the vacuum pressure was maintained below 5 Pa.

MW CCA demonstrates higher yield and ultimate compressive strengths of 2.0 GPa and 2.3 GPa, albeit with a lower fracture strain of 12.1 %

The higher hardness of MW CCA at all tested temperatures aligns with its superior yield strength, indicating a more pronounced contribution from strengthening mechanisms that suppress plastic deformation.
The incorporation of Ti-V or Mo-W into the Cr-Fe-Ni matrix induces significant lattice distortions, generating local stress fields that impede dislocation motion

The interplay of selective solid solution, heterogeneous phase transformations, and localized recrystallization during MA and SPS results in the formation of Ni2Ti4O-type and NiB-type precipitates in TV CCA, whereas MW CCA exhibits CrMoO4-type and Fe2Nb-type precipitates.

The interplay of selective solid solution, heterogeneous phase transformations, and localized recrystallization during MA and SPS results in the formation of Ni2Ti4O-type and NiB-type precipitates in TV CCA, whereas MW CCA exhibits CrMoO4-type and Fe2Nb-type precipitates.
The superior mechanical properties are attributed to the combined contributions of solid solution strengthening, precipitation hardening, and grain boundary/dislocation interactions.
At 800◦C, intensified tribo-oxidation promotes the formation of a stable glaze layer with high oxygen concentrations, mitigating sustained interface degradation.

The secondary reactions among metal oxides, such as the formation of NiNb2O6 and NiWO4, enhance the thermal stability and densification of the tribolayer, thereby culminating in enhanced wear resistance.

MW CCA, with a higher density of strengthening precipitates, exhibits an enhanced yield strength of 2.0 GPa and an ultimate compressive strength of 2.3 GPa, albeit with a reduced fracture strain of 12.1 %.
